A startup failure is recorded where the test that trips over it can read it, because the console cannot carry it: an application that dies on its way up leaves a window with none of its widgets, so the first name a test asks for is missing and "Named GuiWidget not found [Create New Button]" is all that is reported - while the exception that actually killed the boot is written from the boot's own threads, which a test host's per-test console capture files under whichever test it believes is running, and under shard load that is one of the several automation tests waiting their turn for the application gate rather than the one about to fail; that test then passes, and a passing test's captured output is never printed, which is how a stack that WAS written to stderr left no trace at all in a four-shard log (measured: two overlapping tests, a raw-thread write during one lands in the other's output and is lost). StartupFailureLog needs no ambient context - it keeps the last failure in a plain process wide static and writes the type, message and full stack straight to the process's real standard error handle, underneath any per-test redirection, so a run whose test hangs rather than fails still leaves the stack in the log - and every named-widget failure the runner throws now goes through WidgetNotFoundMessage, which appends it, so the shallow symptom carries the deep cause on the row the reader is actually looking at
